newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool indicator rises 2 cents to 722c/kg.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool indicator rises 2 cents to 722c/kg.

text.p: The Australian wool market eastern indicator rose two cents to 722 cents a kg clean on Wednesday at sales in Sydney, Wool International said.
Merino fleece was mixed, with 19/20/24/25 microns unchanged, 21m one percent dearer, 22/23m up to 0.5 percent dearer and 26m 0.5 percent cheaper.
Merino skirtings of 19-22m were up to one percent dearer with light vegetable matter most affected.
Crossbreds of 27-31m were unchanged while in cardings, light carbonising locks were one percent cheaper with crutchings unchanged.
WI said Western Europe and Japanese interests were principal buyers with good support from most sectors of the trade.
Of the 16,375 bales offered, 8.1 percent were passed in.
In early Fremantle trading, merino fleece of 21m was one percent dearer compared to last trading on July 3, with 22m slightly cheaper and 23/24m generally unchanged.
Sales continue on Thursday in Sydney and Fremantle with about 34,770 bales to be offered.
